summary: Vital Orbit is an interactive, mobile friendly decision support web application that helps farmers adapt crop rotations to shifting rainfall and soil moisture conditions using live NASA Earth observations. Users pin a field location on an interactive map, input their local soil type, past two seasons of crops, and farming priorities (saving water, rebuilding soil health, or maximizing income), and dynamically compare three multi-season crop rotation plans.   Powered by the NASA POWER Agroclimatology API (PRECTOTCORR precipitation, T2M temperature, and GWETROOT root-zone soil wetness), Vital Orbit visualizes seasonal moisture gaps and scores candidate rotations using transparent agronomic rules cited from FAO and IITA guidelines. A live Dry Scenario (-25% Rain) toggle allows farmers to stress test rotation resilience under drought assumptions. By translating complex satellite metrics into plain-language tradeoffs while explicitly highlighting data limitations for local agronomist review, Vital Orbit empowers smallholder farmers to protect soil health, conserve water, and reduce climate risk.
details:
How Vital Orbit Works

Vital Orbit is an interactive, browser-based decision support tool that combines live NASA POWER Earth observations with local soil data, crop history, and farmer goals to recommend resilient multi-season crop rotations. The application executes a transparent six-stage pipeline:

Resilient Crop Rotations

  1. Field Input & Geolocation: Users pin their exact field coordinates on an interactive satellite map (or choose from regional agricultural presets across Nigeria's Northern Savanna, Middle Belt, and Southwest) and enter their local soil type (Sandy, Loamy, or Clay), the crops grown over the past two seasons, and weighted priorities (Save Water, Rebuild Soil Health, and Maximize Income).
  2. Live NASA Data Retrieval: The app queries the NASA POWER Agroclimatology API (community=AG) for the pinned latitude and longitude across 2020–2023 to retrieve corrected precipitation (PRECTOTCORR), 2-meter air temperature (T2M), and root-zone soil wetness (GWETROOT).
    Resilient Crop Rotations
  3. Climate Feature Extraction & Dry Scenario Modeling: Raw multi-year measurements are aggregated into seasonal rainfall and soil moisture curves to expose dry-season vulnerability windows. A live Dry Scenario (-25% Rain) toggle applies an explicit 0.75x rainfall assumption to test how each rotation performs under drought stress.
    Resilient Crop Rotations
  4. Transparent Agronomic Scoring Engine: Rather than using an opaque "black-box" model, Vital Orbit evaluates multi-season candidate rotations against a structured crop trait table (grounded in FAO and IITA agronomic guidelines) across three 0–100 sub-scores: Soil Health (rewarding nitrogen-fixing legumes after heavy-feeding cereals and penalizing same-family pest buildup), Water Fit (matching crop drought tolerance to local soil wetness and rainfall), and Priority Fit.
    Resilient Crop Rotations
  5. Plain-Language Explainer & Visual Results: The top three ranked rotation plans are presented with score breakdowns, plain-language explanations of why each sequence fits the field's climate profile, and explicit reminders to validate results with local soil tests and extension officers.
    Resilient Crop Rotations

Key Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Translates Complex Satellite Data into Action: Converts scientific agroclimatology metrics like GWETROOT and PRECTOTCORR into intuitive charts and plain-English crop choices accessible to non-technical farmers.
    Resilient Crop Rotations
  • Protects Soil & Breaks Pest Cycles: Actively discourages continuous monocropping by highlighting bare-soil vulnerability periods and prioritizing nitrogen-fixing legumes (such as cowpea, groundnut, and soybean) alongside drought-resilient cereals and roots.
    Resilient Crop Rotations
  • Proactive Drought Stress-Testing: Empowers farmers and agricultural extension officers to compare normal rainfall baselines against a -25% rainfall dry scenario before committing to seed purchases.
    Resilient Crop Rotations
  • Human-in-the-Loop Safeguards: Reinforces that satellite data (~0.5° grid resolution) supports rather than replaces local farmer judgment, prompting on-the-ground verification of soil pH, drainage, and local market demand.
    Resilient Crop Rotations

Tools, Languages & Resources Used

  • Frontend & Core Logic: HTML5, CSS3 (responsive mobile-first CSS Grid), and Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+).
  • Mapping & Data Visualization: Leaflet.js with Esri World Imagery & Reference map tiles for interactive coordinate pinning, and Chart.js for dual-axis monthly rainfall and root-zone soil wetness visualization.
  • NASA Earth Observation Data: NASA POWER API (https://power.larc.nasa.gov) providing PRECTOTCORR, T2M, and GWETROOT time-series observations.
    Resilient Crop Rotations
  • Agronomic Reference Standards: Crop water requirements, drought tolerance, and nitrogen-fixation traits cited from FAO Crop Water Information and IITA (International Institute of Tropical Agriculture) production guides.

Considerations

  • Explainability: We designed a deterministic, weighted scoring breakdown (soil health, Water Fit, Priority Fit) so farmers and judges can see exact trade-offs when adjusting priorities or toggling drought conditions.
    Resilient Crop Rotations
  • Mobile-Ready Architecture: By running live API queries and client-side scoring directly in lightweight HTML/CSS/JS without heavy server dependencies, the tool works smoothly on both desktop and mobile screens in low-resource settings.
